title: Diffie-Hellman key exchange
summary: Diffie-Hellman (DH) is a key exchange protocol. Two parties agree on a public prime p and generator g. Alice sends A = g^a mod p. Bob sends B = g^b mod p. Both compute shared secret s = B^a = A^b = g^(ab) mod p. Eavesdropper sees g, p, A, B but cannot compute s (discrete logarithm problem). Finite field DH (FFDHE) and elliptic curve DH (ECDH/X25519) are the modern variants.

structure.meaning: Large prime modulus. Must be a safe prime (p = 2q+1 where q is also prime) for security.
Generator of the multiplicative group mod p. Usually 2 or 5.
A = g^a mod p. Sent to Bob.
B = g^b mod p. Sent to Alice.
s = B^a = A^b = g^(ab) mod p. Used as key material (after KDF).
Elliptic curve DH on Curve25519. 32-byte keys, 32-byte shared secret. Faster and simpler than FFDHE.

notes: DH is the foundation of TLS key exchange, SSH, and IPSec.
FFDHE (Finite Field DH) uses large primes (2048+ bits). ECDH (X25519) uses elliptic curves (256 bits, equivalent security).
DH is vulnerable to man-in-the-middle (no authentication). Use with certificates (TLS) or pre-shared keys.
Quantum computers can solve the discrete logarithm problem (Shor's algorithm). Post-quantum alternatives: Kyber (lattice-based).
DH provides forward secrecy: past sessions are secure even if long-term keys are compromised.
